CVE-2026-112712.title: @fastify/middie vulnerable to path-scoped middleware bypass via scope prefix mismatch
CVE-2026-112712.description: @fastify/middie is the Express-style middleware engine for Fastify. In versions from 9.0.0 through 9.3.5, the use() function joined a path-scoped middleware's mount path to the plugin scope prefix in a way that could diverge from the path Fastify's router serves, most often when the scope prefix ended in a slash, and also for array mount paths and for mount paths written without a leading slash. When the two paths disagreed, the middleware was silently skipped while the route handler still ran, so path-scoped middleware such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting could be bypassed by a single unauthenticated request. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.6, and users should upgrade to 9.3.6 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after the router has resolved the request.

CVE-2026-114138.title: Django REST framework: Accept header with many large quoted parameters burns ~19s of CPU per request in content negotiation
CVE-2026-114138.description: Django REST framework is a toolkit for building Web APIs. Prior to 3.18.2, DefaultContentNegotiation.get_accept_list in rest_framework/negotiation.py accepts an unbounded number and aggregate size of Accept tokens, while select_renderer in that file repeatedly invokes _MediaType parsing from rest_framework/utils/mediatypes.py for each attacker-controlled token, every renderer, and forced 406 renegotiation. A remote unauthenticated client can send many distinct media types containing large quoted parameter values with numerous semicolons, causing Django's parameter parser and DRF's repeated parsing structure to consume disproportionate CPU. Requests to any reachable endpoint can pin synchronous workers for prolonged periods, and concurrent requests can make the service unavailable until the requests stop. This issue is fixed in version 3.18.2.

CVE-2026-54427.title: Apache bRPC: Stack Exhaustion via Unbounded Recursion in AMF Parser
CVE-2026-54427.description:
Uncontrolled recursion in the AMF parser in Apache bRPC < 1.18.0 allows a remote RTMP peer to crash a bRPC process by sending deeply nested AMF objects or arrays. The parser recursively processed nested AMF containers without enforcing a depth limit, which could exhaust the native stack.

Affected Scenarios:
Applications using bRPC RTMP support and parsing AMF data from an untrusted RTMP peer. This includes RTMP servers parsing client command messages, RTMP clients parsing server responses or status messages, and either side parsing inbound AMF script data such as metadata or cue points. Direct callers of ReadAMFObject or ReadAMFArray on untrusted input are also affected.

How to Fix:
1. Upgrade Apache bRPC to 1.18.0.
2. Apply the patch from PR https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3344 .

Note:
The fix introduces a configurable AMF nesting depth limit with default value 128. AMF objects or arrays deeper than amf_max_depth are rejected after applying the fix.

Root Cause:
RedisCommandParser::ConsumeImpl rejected negative RESP array counts but accepted zero. It resized the command argument vector to zero elements and continued parsing. In configurations where fatal logs do not abort immediately, execution could continue and write to _args[0] even though the vector was empty.

Deployments that enable ServerOptions.redis_service and accept Redis protocol traffic from untrusted clients. The issue is reached during parsing before command handling or authentication.

CVE-2026-98399.title: s390/ipl: Fix NULL deref in dump_reipl without re-IPL parm block
CVE-2026-98399.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/ipl: Fix NULL deref in dump_reipl without re-IPL parm block

Unlike kdump, which passes the re-IPL parameter block through os_info,
the stand-alone dump passes it through the IPL parm block address and
checksum in lowcore.

Some IPL types, like HMC FTP boot or QEMU direct kernel boot, might not
provide an IPL parameter block. In this case reipl_type_init() selects
IPL_TYPE_UNKNOWN and reipl_block_actual remains NULL. Nevertheless,
dump_reipl_run() unconditionally dereferences it when preparing the
lowcore fields. This may happen to work by chance when address zero
contains readable lowcore data. A zero IPL parameter block address is
then stored in lowcore, causing the stand-alone dumper to enter disabled
wait after completing the dump.

Explicitly store a zero IPL parameter block address and checksum when no
re-IPL parameter block is available. This does not change the behavior:
the stand-alone dumper completes…

CVE-2026-98513.title: drm/nouveau: Fix runtime PM leak in nouveau_connector_detect()
CVE-2026-98513.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/nouveau: Fix runtime PM leak in nouveau_connector_detect()

If nvif_outp_edid_get() fails, nouveau_connector_detect() returns
early without dropping the runtime PM reference taken at the start
of the function, keeping the device powered on until the next
successful detect.

Balance the reference on the error path like the other exit paths
do.

CVE-2026-98566.title: drm/imagination: clamp freelist reconstruction requests
CVE-2026-98566.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/imagination: clamp freelist reconstruction requests

The firmware reconstruction count controls accesses to the request's
fixed freelist ID array and the copy into the fixed response array.
Neither access currently bounds the count to those protocol arrays.

Clamp the count to the request capacity, which is shared by the response
layout, and use that count consistently for reconstruction and response
publication. Keep the firmware recovery exchange instead of dropping an
oversized request without a response, as discussed with the firmware
maintainer.

The issue was found by our static-analysis tool.

CVE-2026-98588.title: bpf, sockmap: Reject max_entries > INT_MAX in sock_map_alloc
CVE-2026-98588.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

bpf, sockmap: Reject max_entries > INT_MAX in sock_map_alloc

sock_map_alloc() only rejects max_entries == 0 and otherwise allows any
u32 value. sock_map_free() then walks the sks[] array with a signed int
iterator:

int i;
for (i = 0; i < stab->map.max_entries; i++)
struct sock **psk = &stab->sks[i];

When a SOCKMAP is created with max_entries = 0xffffffff (UINT_MAX), the
allocation of 32 GiB can succeed on large-memory hosts. During free the
counter reaches 0x80000000, wraps to INT_MIN, is sign-extended by movslq
and turned into a ~16 GiB negative offset from stab->sks, pointing far
below the allocation.

The faulting access is an xchg() write in sock_map_free(). Without
KASAN, the same out-of-bounds write can fault on an unmapped vmalloc page
or corrupt an unrelated allocation if that vmalloc address is populated.

CVE-2026-98841.title: virt: vmgenid: set driver_data before registering notification handlers
CVE-2026-98841.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

virt: vmgenid: set driver_data before registering notification handlers

Both probe paths register their notification handler before assigning
driver_data, which the handler dereferences.

In the devicetree path, the notification IRQ can fire as soon as
devm_request_irq() registers the handler: the interrupt may already be
pending at probe time, for example when a VMM injects the
generation-changed notification while restoring a guest from a snapshot
that was taken before the driver had probed (Firecracker does exactly
this on snapshot restore). The IRQ is also requested with IRQF_SHARED,
so another device sharing the line can trigger the handler just as
early. The handler then calls vmgenid_notify(), which dereferences the
still-NULL driver_data and panics:

Unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at virtual address 0000000000000010
CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 1 Comm: swapper/0 Not tainted 6.18.38+ #1…
